title: Qing’an residents petition county government over heating service
location: Qing’an County Government building, Qing’an County, Suihua, Heilongjiang, China
participants_original: 过百名市民 (over 100 residents, as reported by ON.CC)
threshold_50_evidence: ON.CC reports over 100 residents physically gathered to petition at the county government building, clearly above 50. No exact count or numeric bounds are assigned.

title.summary: Contemporaneous ON.CC headline identifies a county-government gathering over a heating outage.

start_date.summary: Article dated February 5 reports the gathering that Friday, the 5th.

end_date.summary: No gathering end time or date is reported; heat restoration does not establish when the assembly ended.

location.summary: Residents gathered and petitioned at the Qing’an County Government building.

scope.summary: Local gathering at one county government building.

organizer.summary: No organizer is identified in the opened report.

demands.summary: The report describes complaints about inadequate and interrupted heating and a petition at the county government, but does not specify an explicit demand or establish whether the target was government policy or the utility. No existing demand category is assigned.

participants_original.summary: Article says over 100 residents gathered; no exact figure is given.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound assigned from qualitative wording.

participants_max.summary: No exact or upper count reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The opened report explicitly says over 100 residents gathered; this exceeds 50 without an exact headcount.

protester_violence.summary: The report says some residents crossed a police line; it does not describe violence by protesters, and no explicit absence is reported.

state_response.summary: County government announced the heating company would refund two months’ fees to eligible affected residents; the article does not verify completed refunds. Other response fields remain unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Same-day county notice announced a two-month heating-fee refund by the company for eligible affected residents. This records an announced accommodation, not verified payment or victory.

state_response.arrests.summary: Arrests are not established or explicitly ruled out.

state_response.beatings.summary: Beatings are not established or explicitly ruled out.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Crowd dispersal is not established or explicitly ruled out.

state_response.killings.summary: Deaths are not established or explicitly ruled out.

state_response.shootings.summary: Gunfire is not established or explicitly ruled out.

notes: The opened report attributes the heating drop to accidents at Qingxiang Thermal Power Company, reports repairs completed and heat restored, and says the county government announced a two-month fee refund. It does not identify an organizer, quote a specific demand, establish company ownership, verify completed refunds, or show that protesters requested a government policy change. Search-result-only reports add claims about physical scuffles and next-day road closures/testing; those claims are not coded here.
open_questions: Did residents explicitly demand that county authorities enforce or change a government heating policy, or was the gathering directed solely at the utility?
Was the heating provider state-owned, privately operated, or otherwise subject to a specific government policy in February 2021?
Were the announced refunds delivered, and did residents continue gathering or take further action after February 5?
What was the exact attendance and who organized or coordinated the gathering?
Did police arrest, beat, disperse, or otherwise act against participants? The opened article does not resolve these fields.
Are the Hope Voice-derived reports of physical contact and February 6 road closures/testing independently corroborated?
